LESSON: MEASURING AND MARKING OUT TOOLS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Tools and Production
Topic 4.1: Measuring and Marking Out Tools
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Measuring and Marking Out Tools, part of Tools and Production in Grade 7 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why are measuring and marking out tools important in day-to-day life? 2. How are measuring and marking out tools used when performing tasks?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use visual aids and realia to identify measuring tools (tape measure, steel rule, callipers, weighing balance, stopwatch, ammeter, voltmeter) and marking out tools (divider, try-square, marking gauge, dot punch, scriber, pencil, marking knife),

2. choose the appropriate measuring and marking out tools to perform a given task,

3. use available resources to search for information on the use of measuring and marking out tools,

4. perform specific tasks using measuring and marking out tools,

5. practice caring for measuring and marking out tools. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use visual aids and realia to identify measuring tools (tape measure, steel rule, callipers, weighing balance, stopwatch, ammeter, voltmeter) and marking out tools (divider, try-square, marking gauge, dot punch, scriber, pencil, marking knife),
2. choose the appropriate measuring and marking out tools to perform a given task,
3. use available resources to search for information on the use of measuring and marking out tools,
4. perform specific tasks using measuring and marking out tools,
5. practice caring for measuring and marking out tools. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Measuring and Marking Out Tools together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner develops explanation, evaluation, and decision-making skills when choosing

the appropriate measuring and marking out tools to perform a given task.

• Self-efficacy: learner develops self-awareness skills by showing a concerted attention to detail when performing specific

tasks using measuring and marking out tools.

Values:
• Respect: learner shows open-mindedness when discussing the use of measuring and marking out tools in the immediate

environment.

• Responsibility: learner shows accountability by caring for measuring and marking out tools in the immediate environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Disaster Risk Reduction: learner avoids situations that can lead to injuries when caring for measuring and marking out tools in

the immediate environment.

Link to other Subjects:

Mathematics: learner enhances the skill of measurement when performing specific tasks using measuring and marking out tools.
